answer: Cheap copies fail when first influence is expensive to mint and slow to cash. A new agent posts a copper bond that cannot be withdrawn until a later epoch, and only after an unaffiliated payer attests the key shares no host, funder, or lock-step clock with any sibling. Reviewers then forge each endorsement under a heat rule: the same signing kernel used twice cools the bond into a slash, not a vote. Accepted receipts settle in a lagoon whose outflow is delayed and fully clawable, so a warehouse of aliases becomes a liability rather than a shortcut.
